中东停火破裂后美军突然收手！BTC $64,968要见底反弹了？

事件概述

简单给大家捋一下，就在刚才，市场爆出美国暂停了对伊朗的军事打击。虽然之前中东的停火协议闹掰了，但美军这波突然“踩刹车”，说白了就是在给局势降温。老美不想把事态进一步搞大，这对全球风险资产来说，绝对是个喘息的窗口。对咱们币圈来说，悬在头顶的地缘政治利空剑暂时摘下来了。

深度解读

为什么这条新闻重要？

做交易不能光看表面，得看底牌。前段时间中东那边打生打死，避险情绪飙升，各路资金吓得跑去抱团黄金或者现金，加密市场被抽水抽得很惨。美军这次暂停打击，根本原因在于各方势力在幕后重新博弈，老美目前承受不起一场全面中东战争的通胀反噬。

在整个大盘周期里，现在属于洗盘末期，市场其实不缺钱，缺的就是做多信心。地缘冲突就是压制盘面最大的那座大山。这次踩刹车，意味着短期的“战争溢价”要被迅速挤出了。资金的风险偏好会快速修复，之前因为怕打仗而观望的机构资金，这下终于敢进场干活了。这也跟近期大盘企稳反弹的节奏完全对得上，外部环境一稳，加密市场就能回归自身的逻辑。

对市场的影响

短期来看，避险情绪消退等于直接给大盘喂了一口猛药。大家看盘面，BTC现在交投在$64,968.54附近，24小时微微涨了0.64%，说明已经有聪明钱在提前抢跑。恐慌情绪一旦消散，这种涨幅肯定是不够的，后续大概率会迎来情绪宣泄式的补涨。

更猛的是ETH，目前报价$1,948.45，24小时直接拉升了3.16%。老韭菜都知道，ETH这阵子被压抑得太惨了，一旦外部风险解除，以太坊这种高弹性的资产往往会有报复性反弹。从历史经验看，每次地缘冲突出现实质性缓和，风险资产都会走出一波连续上攻的走势。那些之前因为避险流出的稳定币，会像饿狼一样扑回市场抢筹码。

操作思路

🎯 影响预判
- 币种：BTC / ETH
- 方向：利多📈 预测涨
- 时长：BTC 12小时 / ETH 24小时

💡 讲真，这波我看多。外部最大利空解除，空头现在唯一的底气没了，随时可能发生踩踏式平仓。BTC只要站稳$64,968.54上方，就会打开向上的空间；而ETH刚起势，盯着$1,948.45能不能守住，守住了就能继续冲。别总想着摸顶做空，顺势接多才是正道。

Whether you’ve been in crypto for 3 days or 3 years, the market has a funny way of teaching us all the exact same lessons. If you want to survive (and actually profit), keep these in mind:

Rule: If it’s already trending everywhere, you’re likely late. Wait for the pullback.

Strategy stops buying Bitcoin for five consecutive weeks! What signal does MSTR’s $540 million cash-out release?

In one sentence
Strategy hasn’t bought any coins for five straight weeks—and it has also sold $540 million worth of MSTR stock to build up cash reserves, leaving a short-term shortage of fresh funds to take over BTC.

What’s going on
Guys, the Strategy that always “buys the dip no matter what” has finally stalled. For five straight weeks—over a month—there hasn’t been a single BTC purchase. Not only did they stop buying, they even flipped and sold $544.5 million worth of MSTR stock. To put it simply, they’ve converted their company stock holdings into cash. Their U.S. dollar cash reserves have now piled up to $3.75 billion.

This kind of move would have been unthinkable before. This company used to be all but trying to dump every dollar into BTC. Now they’ve suddenly turned around to hoard cash. On one hand, they might feel the current BTC price isn’t attractive enough and they don’t want to “catch the bag.” On the other hand, more likely they’re preparing defensively—keeping plenty of ammo for the winter.

Impact on the market
Honestly, this is a major blow to short-term market sentiment. Strategy has consistently been one of the biggest buyers in the market, and many retail investors treat their increased holdings as a bellwether. Now the largest buyer has pulled back, and at the $65,025.99 level, BTC has lost its strongest source of funding support.

- Short term: The market has lost a key “price cushion” buyer. If other institutions also wait and see, buy-side strength will quickly fade, making liquidity look thin.
- Medium term: The $375 million cash reserve feels like a question mark. This money could be deployed into the market at any time to buy the dip—but as long as they don’t act, it signals that management doesn’t think the current price is cheap enough, keeping ongoing pressure on the overall order book.

My take
My view is clear: bearish in the short term—don’t rush to catch a falling knife. Even the most “diamond hands” are cashing out for defense, which suggests they see short-term risks. If BTC breaks below the $65,025.99 support level, there’s still plenty of downside room—don’t be a hero and try to hold through it. Even though ETH is currently around $1,949.23 and looks a bit more resilient, if the broader market truly dumps lower, it won’t escape either. Be patient and wait until Strategy spends that $375 million. Then, they’ll be the real pack leader. If they don’t move, we just watch.

深度解读

老铁们，重点不是"无人机"三个字，是"伊朗支持"。

伊朗系民兵打沙特，这不是普通的武装骚扰，背后是两个中东大国的代理人博弈。2022年俄乌冲突刚爆发时，BTC先砸后暴力反弹，因为全球资金突然意识到：你需要一个不被任何政府冻结、不受银行系统限制的避险通道。现在同样的剧本又在演。

再往深想一层：如果沙特和伊朗关系彻底恶化，霍尔木兹海峡航运受影响，油价暴涨→通胀预期回升→美联储降息计划又要搁置。这条链路短期利好BTC避险叙事，但如果演变成全球性危机，所有风险资产都会被波及，币圈也跑不了。

参考今年4月伊朗直接打击以色列那次，BTC在48小时内从$62,000附近冲上$65,000以上，然后逐步回落。这次如果沙特不进行大规模军事反击，脉冲式上涨之后大概率还会回踩。

Uncover the truth of the crypto world: trading is never a win-win—it’s capital redistribution

Many people over-glamorize BTC and ETH trades, piling on technical analysis, financial visions, and talk of future value. In reality, it’s all packaged hype. The most naked essence of the crypto world has never been mutual benefit and win-win outcomes—it’s a brutal game of capital redistribution.

Most retail traders lose money not because they misread the market, but because they’re in the wrong tier. Same market, same bullish judgment—if a retail account bets $50 with a $300 account, while a big player with a $100,000 position also risks $50 trying the same trade.
With a small pin-prick spike or pullback and washout, retail traders get liquidated and exit with their principal wiped out—zeroed. The big player’s position takes no real damage; after the market recovers, they continue to harvest. The moment you get crushed and leave the game is when the main players’ real trade begins.
The core of making money in crypto has never been about perfectly accurate judgment—it’s about who can last longer and who has stronger risk resistance. Small money is destined to be harvested; big money can survive steadily. Even if your trading ideas are identical, retail traders will always be the hunted.
Stop fantasizing that you’re trading with the trend. Most retail traders are simply part of the market’s liquidity supply. When you’re emotionally hyped and chase at the top, the main players ride the trend to distribute and exit; when you panic in despair and cut losses to stop out, the main players seize the opportunity to accumulate at low prices.
Retail greed and fear are the market’s most stable source of profit. Crypto is not a gentle investment arena—it’s a hellish battlefield where the weak are prey. Once you understand this survival logic and step out of retail thinking, you can gradually transform from prey into someone who feeds.

Options traders collectively shed their armor! BTC $65,100 hedged positions cleared ahead of the Fed

In one sentence
The options market has seen a sharp withdrawal of bearish positions, bullish sentiment is heating up, and BTC and ETH are being briefly boosted.

What happened
Bro, put simply, big money has pulled all its “insurance” ahead of the Fed meeting. The Put/Call ratio in the options market was smashed from 0.76 at the end of June to 0.52. What does that mean? Previously, during the big drop, everyone was疯狂ly buying put protection—but now they’re not buying it anymore. These aren’t small retail traders; they’re real, large players with serious capital. They’re willing to “bare it all” before the July 28–29 FOMC meeting, which suggests they’re confident. Meanwhile, BTC’s one-period implied volatility has been compressed to 34.3%, far below 40.8% over six months—meaning the market believes there won’t be any major turbulence in the near term. The 25-delta skew has also fallen to around 4%, and that effectively signals a breakdown of defensive positioning.

Impact on the market
In the short term, when options whales collectively unwind hedges, it’s like loosening the market’s restraints. BTC is now $65,100.01, and ETH has already risen to $1,954.41 (24h +3.48%). This de-risking can create a mild tailwind. Since market makers previously accumulated a large amount of put options for hedging, once those positions are closed, they don’t need to keep selling spot “to save themselves.” Instead, they may even rebalance and buy back some longs. However, don’t get too excited: with volatility pushed this low, if the Fed meeting delivers anything even slightly beyond expectations, both up and down moves could get violent.

In the medium term, the market is in a calm before the storm. Even though the options market is relatively optimistic, the consensus is too uniform—everyone thinks the meeting will be safe. That, by itself, is a risk point.

My view
To be honest, I’m moderately bullish in this move, but I wouldn’t blindly chase. At BTC’s $65,100.01 level, overhead resistance is clear. Options data is a positive (bullish) signal—whales backed it with real money—but with volatility this low, I don’t recommend going all-in on betting on direction at this point. ETH is up 3.48% today to $1,954.41 and is outperforming the broader market; short-term momentum is still there. The safest play is to wait until the Fed meeting lands, and don’t fiddle with things before it. If you must trade, keep it light and follow the trend—make sure your stop-loss is in place, because when low-volatility conditions suddenly burst, there’s no room for error from “needles” (spikes).

Babylon didn’t open its own lending shop. Instead, I think this move is the right one.
If you had a native BTC collateral technology in your hands, what would you do?

Many projects would probably just build another lending platform on the side, bundling everything—wallets, capital pools, interest rates, and token incentives—within their own ecosystem. The story sounds complete, but users and liquidity still have to be built from scratch.

@babylonlabs_io  This time, it didn’t do that.

It first integrates Trustless Bitcoin Vaults (TBV) into Aave V4: Babylon keeps native BTC on Bitcoin and makes it verifiable collateral, while the lending protocol handles borrowing terms, how interest is calculated, and where liquidity comes from.$BABY #baby 

Honestly, I really like this division of labor.

What BTC users truly lack may not be the tenth new lending website, but a path that can plug into existing financial applications—without requiring them to convert BTC into wrapped tokens first. If Babylon paves that way, it won’t need to compete with every app for business each time. Lending platforms, stablecoins, and other products can keep doing what they’re good at, while Babylon focuses on solving how native BTC can safely participate.

This is also an upside for $BABY  that’s easier to understand than “launching another feature.”

BABY already covers the Gas, governance, and network security use cases for Babylon Genesis. What’s really worth watching going forward isn’t how many “shops” Babylon can open by itself, but how many applications are willing to plug the native BTC entry point into this ecosystem. The more integrations there are, the more likely the surrounding demand for network security, governance, and ecosystem collaboration will grow stronger.#ETH  

Of course, it’s still an open testnet for now, and Aave V4 is also an app that’s already available for experience in the current stage—still far from real-scale usage.

But at least this route hasn’t made me feel like Babylon is reinventing the wheel. It’s more like fixing a road, so that capital that would otherwise be stuck in Bitcoin can go do more things elsewhere.

What I want to see now is: which is the next application willing to take this path?

But since net inflow is still positive, it suggests there’s larger capital behind the scenes that keeps “building positions.” This is how Wall Street plays it—letting retail investors see that someone is selling to create fear, while they quietly accumulate.

With BTC sitting at $65,275—not exactly high, but also not a bottom—if institutions are willing to keep adding here, fundamentally they’re positioning for what comes next. While there’s still some noise on the regulatory front, the ETF itself is a product of regulatory loosening. The bigger direction is already locked in and not reversible.

It’s different from the frenzy right after spot ETFs were approved. Now we’re in a more rational accumulation phase. This kind of slow-and-steady bull-market style inflow is healthier than a short-term, blow-off rally.

Impact on the Market

In the short term, holding above $65,275 is a signal. Three consecutive weeks of net inflows inject confidence into the market. ETH’s rise of 4.21% today to $1,965 also indicates that capital is moving back toward large-cap market leaders, not mindlessly chasing random altcoins.

The medium-term impact is even more crucial. Ongoing ETF inflows mean traditional financial capital is treating BTC as a standard allocation asset—not coming in to bet and then leave. Once this trend takes shape, it’s unlikely to reverse in the short run.

You can look at gold ETF approval as a reference: when it first launched, volatility was high and controversy was everywhere. But over a longer time horizon, ETF inflows become the foundation for a long-term bull run. BTC is basically following the same path.

Gold broke above $4,100 and silver is back above $60. Inflation panic and the return-to-hard-assets sentiment have significantly diverted funds that might otherwise have flowed into crypto.

#baby Recently, I’ve been going hard on the details, and @babylonlabs_io in the whitepaper—Section 3 has a setup that really leaves me with a sore throat: “The giant whales run their own nodes for encryption, while the small fry outsource the work to professional institutions.”

Take a closer look: the bar really is designed to force you to bow your head. A single machine has to handle 43GB of data and still compute for 20 minutes. A typical player puts up 0.1 BTC as collateral; at most they can borrow only a few thousand U of liquidity. If they also pay electricity to buy servers, they probably won’t even earn back enough to cover a basic bowl of pork rice. The official “solution” is to offer an “outsourcing” option—but with this concession, the “absolute decentralization” filter that was originally touted breaks into pieces.

Let’s put it another way. You spend a fortune installing a top-notch anti-theft vault, but your house can’t fit it, so you end up putting it in the building’s security guard room. The protocol is written plainly: without your required multisig, the guard absolutely can’t walk off with the assets inside. The principal’s safety is preserved, but operational control is completely handed over.

Time is the lifeline: if something unexpected happens, you must submit the dispute proof within an extremely short window.

Human error becomes the crux: at that point, all you can do is pray the guard doesn’t doze off and doesn’t go offline. If they fumble and miss the timing—leading to your staked collateral being locked—who’s going to take the blame?

Fast forward to Section 10, where $BABY  is defined as ecosystem fuel and a voting scepter. The likely future script is: custodial intermediaries must lock $BABY  just to take orders; if they do a bad job, their deposit gets seized. In theory it’s airtight, but in reality it’s harsh.

So who swings the sanction hammer? Voters—who hold the coins.

Chain of interests underwrites capture: in crypto, top nodes are often also giant whales holding the most coins. Expect these people to hold meetings and vote to punish themselves by confiscating their own real money? That’s like the left hand judging the right hand—highly dramatic hammer raised, but it usually lands softly in the end.

To grow the ecosystem, introducing a delegation mechanism is a pragmatic compromise—I absolutely understand that. But insisting on coating this model with a veneer of “fully trustless” gold is a bit too much, like trying to hoodwink people. The moment you hand the core data to a third-party server, even if the code says “can’t do evil,” the risk of “maliciously passive negligence” at the operations layer has already been planted deep.

Don’t let those dazzling “non-custodial” concepts dizzy you. The assets aren’t leaving your hands—that’s one thing. But drawing your sword still requires someone else’s help; that’s the fatal weakness. If you’re going to play in this space, DYOR.#eth $ETH

#baby  flips through @babylonlabs_io  the whitepaper, and in Section 3 there’s a setup that makes me think deeply: it says that large holders can generate the encrypted circuits on their own, guaranteeing absolute trustlessness; but small retail users are constrained by hard thresholds, basically leaving this work to professional institutions.

From the perspective of an ordinary user: putting up 0.1 BTC as collateral to obtain a few thousand U in liquidity—if you insist on running the node yourself, the mere burden of carrying the 43GB storage load and a 20-minute computation time would make the high operational and maintenance costs wipe out the meager returns.

The “delegation” solution proposed by the official documentation is a compromise. But once this loophole is opened, the original pure vision of decentralization gets twisted.

The whitepaper repeatedly emphasizes that, because it requires users to co-sign, third-party institutions absolutely cannot move your Bitcoin. The principal is indeed safe; the core issue is that retail users effectively hand over the protocol’s “response control” to others.

The time-critical gate: in the event of a dispute within the lending protocol, a challenge proof must be submitted within a strictly limited time window.

Single point of failure: at this moment, retail users can only fully rely on the custodial institution’s servers not going down. If the institution’s network is slow or—worse—intentionally stalls, causing the proof window to be missed, the funds can get locked or trigger system-level penalties. Who’s responsible for this bad debt?

Now look at Section 10: $BABY  is granted the dual attributes of Gas and governance. The future game model is clear: nodes must stake $BABY  to take on work; violations result in forfeiting the deposit. The original design intention is good, but there’s a fatal paradox:

Judge and player are the same: the punishment mechanism requires token holders to vote to execute it. But in the crypto ecosystem, nodes with monopolistic computing power are often also token-rich oligarchs. Expecting these entrenched beneficiaries to “do the right thing” and vote against their own interests—willingly forfeiting their real money to punish themselves—may be too idealistic.

To balance network scale and user experience, introducing proxy nodes is an extremely practical business decision, and there’s nothing wrong with that. But if you continue to brand this compromise as “fully trustless,” it’s a bit of a way to dodge the hard parts. The moment you’re forced to store underlying data on someone else’s servers, the code-level “can’t do evil” already yields to the real operational trust crisis. In the face of all kinds of non-custodial narratives, everyone must stay clear-headed and insist on DYOR.#eth $ETH

深度解读

为什么这条新闻重要？
讲真，很多人看这种国际新闻可能觉得跟币圈没直接关系，但背后的资金逻辑绝不是这么算的。首先，莫斯科把这事儿拔高到“恐怖主义”的定性，这就不是普通的军事交锋了，这等于为俄罗斯接下来采取更激进、更不对称的报复措施铺好了路。周末市场流动性本来就偏差，任何一点火星子都可能引发连环爆仓。

目前在宏观周期里，全球资金都在等美联储接下来的动作，市场情绪属于惊弓之鸟。在这个节骨眼上突发的地缘冲突升级，往往会瞬间改变资金的避险偏好。之前几次地区冲突升级，加密市场都是先跌为敬。这不仅是风险资产的情绪降温，更是主力资金借机洗盘的绝佳借口。

Many people think “decentralization” is like a home light switch—you just press the button and everything is settled. But think back to basic physics: textbooks often assume everything is “perfectly frictionless,” yet once you put it on real asphalt, as soon as the tires wear down and slip, the brakes and chassis will inevitably lose control. Cross-chain networks are the same: to establish real consensus on-chain, every step upward has to overcome immense resistance.

When I deeply read the ninth section of the @babylonlabs_io  whitepaper, that repeatedly mentioned “Bitcoin light client” finally made their playbook against this resistance crystal clear. It sounds ordinary, but it is precisely the “keystone” of the entire cross-chain vault infrastructure. A light client’s cleverness lies in its refusal to touch those hundreds of gigabytes of bloated full-node data; it only fetches block headers, using Merkle proofs to verify the authenticity of transactions. Whether it’s the subsequent issuance of collBTC or the circulation of stablecoins, everything relies on this “foreman” watching in real time—confirming that your assets are firmly locked in the Bitcoin mainnet. #baby 

However, hard-core mechanisms often come with high costs. Every time you expand to a new network, you have to spin up a batch of new validating nodes. Server operation and bandwidth usage—these are real money paid out, no matter how you look at it. Relying on people “doing it out of love” won’t get you far; how do you balance the books? Turn to the tenth section on the economic model of $BABY , and the answer surfaces. During the project’s early cold-start period, BABY’s distribution is essentially used as a kind of “settling-in allowance” to reward and support the underlying maintenance providers. You act as a sentinel for the protocol, and the protocol pays you back with tokens to cover your costs.

Looking at a single light node, it seems dry and unremarkable. But when hundreds or thousands of nodes intertwine across dozens of ecosystems, that invisible network becomes the vault’s most solid armor. Once the whole system becomes active, the real transaction fees generated by the network can cover the early token emissions—only then does this flywheel truly get running. Therefore, the price expectation of $BABY  is absolutely not empty hype; it is the silent, day-by-day contribution of countless nodes. In Web3, achieving “no trust required” ultimately means you still have to pay—only that the settlement unit changes, from cash into Token. #eth $ETH

在深读 @babylonlabs_io 白皮书第九部分时，那个被反复提及的“Bitcoin light client”（比特币轻客户端），让我彻底看清了他们应对这种阻力的底牌。这东西听起来平平无奇，却恰恰是整套跨链金库设施的“定海神针”。轻客户端的聪明之处在于，它坚决不碰那几百个G的臃肿全节点数据，只抓取区块头，凭借梅克尔证明来敲定交易的真实性。无论是后续 collBTC 的发行，还是稳定币的流转，全靠这位“监工”在现场盯着，确认你的资产死死锁在比特币主网里。#baby 

然而，硬核机制往往伴随着高昂的开销。每拓展一个新的网络，就得拉起一批新的验证节点。服务器运转、带宽占用，这些都是割肉般的真金白银。靠爱发电注定走不远，这笔账该怎么平？翻到第十节关于 $BABY 的经济模型，答案就浮出水面了。在项目刚起步的冷启动期，BABY的发放本质上就是用来打赏底层维护者的“安家费”。你替协议当哨兵，协议就拿代币补偿你的成本。

单独审视一个轻节点，似乎干巴巴的没什么意思。可当成百上千个节点在数十个生态里互相交织，那张无形的网就成了金库最坚硬的铠甲。等整个盘子活络起来，网络产生的真实手续费能覆盖掉早期的代币增发，这套飞轮才算真正跑通。因此，$BABY 的价格预期绝不是炒作出来的空气，是无数节点日复一日的静默付出。在 Web3 想要做到“无需信任”，终归是要掏钱的，只不过结账的筹码换成了 Token。#eth $ETH

title: Ethereum Awakens: The Silent Whale Movement That Could Shape ETH Next Move
subTitle:
Something unusual is happening beneath the surface of Ethereum. The price moves like every other day, candles rise and fall, traders argue over charts, and social media chases the next headline. Yet the real story is unfolding where very few people are looking. Fresh wallets have appeared. Massive amounts of capital have quietly flowed into ETH. No celebration. No loud announcement. Just patient accumulation. It feels less like speculation and more like preparation for something that has not fully arrived.

The first clue came when anonymous whale wallets bought millions worth of ETH within a short period. Then another mystery unfolded. A single whale used more than fifty million DAI to collect over twenty five thousand ETH at an average price near nineteen hundred sixty eight. These purchases were not scattered across old trading accounts. They moved through newly created wallets, almost as if someone wanted every step to begin with a clean page. The pattern tells a deeper story. This is not the behavior of traders searching for a quick profit. It looks like a carefully planned strategy built with patience.

Ethereum has always been more than a digital asset. It is a living network where smart contracts carry ideas from one person to another like veins carrying life through a body. Liquidity keeps the system moving, allowing value to flow without stopping. Governance gives the network its voice, letting communities shape the future instead of waiting for permission from a central authority. Every new application, every decentralized exchange, every lending platform becomes another heartbeat inside this growing digital ecosystem.

When large investors choose to accumulate ETH, they are not simply buying a token. They are buying access to the engine that powers thousands of decentralized applications. They are placing confidence in a network that continues to evolve while supporting developers, creators, and businesses around the world. Every major purchase becomes another signal that the foundation is considered valuable even before the next chapter begins.

For traders, this creates a different perspective. Price action may still move with volatility, but large accumulation often changes the emotional landscape. Fear begins to lose its grip when powerful buyers continue adding to their positions instead of selling. Builders also find confidence in these moments because long term capital usually supports innovation rather than short lived excitement. The network grows stronger as more people choose to create instead of simply trade.

The coordinated appearance of new wallets adds another layer to the mystery. Institutions and professional investors often separate assets across multiple addresses for security and operational reasons. When several fresh wallets begin collecting ETH around similar price levels, it suggests planning rather than coincidence. Each wallet becomes another piece of a much larger picture that is only beginning to reveal itself.

No one can promise the next move with certainty. Markets remain unpredictable, and even the strongest signals can be challenged by global events. Yet history often shows that patient accumulation appears before the crowd fully understands what is happening. By the time the headlines become obvious, much of the opportunity has already passed.

Perhaps this is why Ethereum continues to attract attention from the largest players. They are not only investing in today's market. They are investing in tomorrow's digital infrastructure, where finance, artificial intelligence, gaming, identity, and global commerce become increasingly connected. In that future, Ethereum is not just another blockchain. It becomes part of the foundation where humans and intelligent machines collaborate, exchange value, and build systems that operate without borders. The whales may simply be seeing that future before everyone else.

title: Does Arthur Hayes’ Latest ETH Buy Really Signal a Market Bottom?
subTitle:
Many crypto investors follow the wallets of experienced traders.
The reason is simple. They want to know where smart money is going before the rest of the market catches up.
Recently, Arthur Hayes has been buying Ethereum again. On-chain data shows he has added nearly 3,900 ETH, worth around $7.5 million, over the past few weeks.
This has led many people to ask the same question.
Has Ethereum already reached its bottom?
The truth is, no one can know for sure.
A single investor, no matter how experienced, cannot determine where the market will go next. Even professional investors sometimes buy before the price falls further.
So why do people pay attention to these purchases?
Because experienced investors usually think differently.
Instead of trying to buy at the exact lowest price, they look for assets they believe are undervalued. If they expect the investment to perform well over the next few years, buying slightly early doesn’t matter as much.
This is called accumulation.
Rather than making one huge purchase, investors often buy in smaller amounts over time. This helps reduce the risk of entering the market at the wrong moment.
Ethereum also has a few factors working in its favor. A large amount of ETH is locked in staking, which reduces the number of coins available for trading. Many long-term holders also continue to hold their positions despite market volatility.
However, none of these factors guarantee that the price can’t fall further.
Crypto prices are affected by many things, including investor sentiment, global liquidity, economic conditions, and demand from institutions. These factors can have a bigger impact than the actions of one investor.
This is why experienced investors never rely on a single signal.
They combine on-chain data, market trends, trading volume, and macroeconomic conditions before making a decision.
The biggest lesson isn’t whether Arthur Hayes is right or wrong.
It’s understanding how professional investors approach the market. They focus on long-term value, manage risk carefully, and build positions gradually instead of trying to perfectly time every trade.
That’s a strategy every crypto investor can learn from.

1. Lido advances large-scale architecture upgrade
The liquid staking protocol Lido is migrating more than 8 million stETH to the new validator architecture after the Pectra upgrade. This is expected to reduce the number of Ethereum validators by roughly one-third and cut the volume of validation messages per epoch across the network by about 29%. The update also introduces the CMv2 mechanism, requiring node operators to lock ETH as performance collateral, further evolving its core staking system toward stronger risk controls and higher efficiency.  

2. BlackRock speaks out: Crypto assets can withstand quantum threats
In its latest report, BlackRock notes that upgrading cryptography to defend against quantum attacks is currently far easier than building quantum computers capable of breaking Bitcoin’s cryptographic system. The report emphasizes that, at present, no machines can break Bitcoin cryptography, though some BTC may carry potential risk due to exposed public keys. Meanwhile, BlackRock, together with institutions such as Coinbase and Fidelity Digital Assets, is advancing a Bitcoin Security Alliance to strengthen the industry’s forward-looking planning for quantum safety.  

3. Kimi K3 open-sources core components, strengthening agent training capabilities
After the Kimi.ai team released open weights for the Kimi K3 model and accompanying technical reports, it continued to open-source core infrastructure such as MoonEP, AgentENV, and FlashKDA. These cover distributed MoE training, agent environment orchestration, and high-performance attention kernels. The official statement says these components could reduce communication and inference costs in large-scale training, and can also serve as plug-and-play backends for flash-linear-attention—adding new variables to the competition for AI-and-crypto integrated infrastructure.  

4. Progress in US–Iran talks stirs expectations for risk assets
US President Trump said the US is conducting intensive negotiations with Iran, but the window is limited. If talks break down, the US may restart tough military actions. According to public data, nearly 300 Hong Kong-listed companies have continued to increase share buybacks in recent times, with leading names such as Tencent, AIA, and Xiaomi especially active. Event Overview

Guys, this is really something. Qatar and Pakistan, acting as intermediaries between the U.S. and Iran, have pushed the negotiations forward by a step. The most crucial point—Iran has agreed to use Bitcoin to pay the transit fee for the Strait of Hormuz. In plain terms, the world’s key choke point for global oil shipping is starting to accept BTC settlements. When a sovereign nation uses BTC for international trade payments, the symbolic significance far outweighs the actual amount.

In-Depth Interpretation

Why is this news important?

Honestly, many people haven’t fully reacted to the weight of this headline.

First layer of logic: Iran has been under sanctions for years, and the dollar system has basically been locked down for it. Using BTC for settlement isn’t following trends—it’s a real, urgent need. This shows that in an extreme geopolitical environment, crypto has upgraded from “speculation tool” to “financial infrastructure.”

Second layer of logic: The Strait of Hormuz isn’t some minor waterway. About one-third of seaborne oil shipments globally pass through it. If Iran truly begins collecting transit fees in BTC, it means energy-trade funding flows would be directly funneled into the crypto market. This isn’t Wall Street’s paper game like an ETF—this is real, on-chain demand paid in hard money.

Third layer of logic: Looking at the current cycle, BTC has been grinding around $64,595 repeatedly, and the market lacks exactly a new narrative catalyst. The ETF story has been going on for more than a year—people are starting to get aesthetically fatigued. Suddenly, a “sovereign state using BTC for energy settlement” emerges, and that’s far more explosive than any ETF inflow data.

Also, don’t ignore one more thing: If there’s genuine progress in the U.S.–Iran negotiations, Middle East geopolitical risk would cool down. Some of the capital that previously rushed into gold and U.S. Treasuries due to risk-off sentiment may reallocate back into risk assets.

Market Impact

In the short term, this news directly boosts market sentiment. BTC is now at $64,595 and has only fallen 0.28% over the past 24 hours, which suggests the market hasn’t priced in this positive catalyst yet. Once the news starts spreading and building momentum, short-term capital could rush in quickly.

ETH is currently at $1,930.78, up 0.96% in the past 24 hours, but the move isn’t that large. If BTC lifts on this news, ETH catching up is highly likely. However, its upside may be less elastic than BTC—after all, this news directly reinforces BTC’s “digital gold” and “sovereign settlement currency” narrative.

Mid-term impact is even deeper. If Iran sets this precedent, will other sanctioned countries follow? Russia and Venezuela, for example, have every incentive to do the same. More importantly, this could force the U.S. and Europe to accelerate the rollout of crypto regulatory frameworks—because if you don’t regulate it properly, your geopolitical rivals will use it first.

For historical reference, look at 2021 when El Salvador announced BTC as legal tender. Back then, market sentiment was instantly ignited. Although that time came with a bull-market cycle tailwind, the point is: when sovereign-level adoption of BTC happens, every occurrence becomes a major narrative milestone.

📰 伊朗接受比特币支付过境费！BTC $64,595这次真要起飞？

事件概述

老铁们，这事真的炸裂。卡塔尔和巴基斯坦当中间人，帮美国和伊朗的谈判往前推了一步。最关键的点——伊朗同意用比特币收霍尔木兹海峡的过境费！说白了，全球石油运输的咽喉要道，现在开始接受BTC结算了。一个主权国家用BTC做国际贸易支付，这事的象征意义远大于实际金额。

深度解读

为什么这条新闻重要？

讲真，这条新闻的分量很多人还没反应过来。

第一层逻辑：伊朗被制裁这么多年，美元体系对它基本锁死了。用BTC结算不是赶时髦，是实打实的刚需。这说明在极端地缘政治环境下，加密货币已经从"投机工具"升级成"金融基础设施"了。

第二层逻辑：霍尔木兹海峡不是小河沟，全球大约三分之一的海运石油从这里经过。如果伊朗真开始用BTC收过境费，意味着能源贸易资金流会直接灌入加密市场。这不是ETF那种华尔街纸面博弈，是真金白银的链上需求。

第三层逻辑：放在当前周期看，BTC在$64,595附近反复磨，市场缺的就是新叙事催化剂。ETF的故事讲了一年多了，大家有点审美疲劳。突然冒出来一个"主权国家用BTC做能源结算"，这比任何ETF流入数据都有爆炸性。

而且别忽略一点：美伊谈判如果有实质性进展，中东地缘风险降温，之前因为避险情绪跑到黄金和美债里的资金，部分会重新分配到风险资产。

对市场的影响

短期来看，这个消息直接提振市场情绪。BTC现在$64,595，24小时才跌了0.28%，说明市场还没定价这个利好。一旦消息开始扩散发酵，短线资金会快速涌入。

ETH当前$1,930.78，24小时涨了0.96%但幅度不算大。如果BTC因为这条消息拉升，ETH跟涨是大概率事件，但弹性可能不如BTC——毕竟这新闻直接强化的是BTC的"数字黄金"和"主权结算货币"叙事。

中期影响更深远。伊朗如果开了这个头，其他被制裁的国家会不会跟？俄罗斯、委内瑞拉这些国家完全有动力效仿。更关键的是，这会倒逼美国和欧洲加速出台加密监管框架——你不规范它，你的地缘对手就会先利用它。

历史参考可以看2021年萨尔瓦多宣布BTC为法定货币，当时市场情绪直接被点燃。虽然那次有牛市周期加持不能简单类比，但主权层面接纳BTC这件事，每次出现都是重大叙事节点。

操作思路

- 时长：BTC 12小时 / ETH 24小时

Last night I went through the TBV liquidation workflow of @babylonlabs_io  again. What truly made me stop wasn’t “whether BTC can be lent out as stablecoins,” but a seemingly dumb yet actually crucial detail: a Vault is not an account balance—it’s a complete UTXO.

This means risk handling can’t work like ordinary DeFi positions where you can slice off collateral in whatever amount you want to sell. Each TBV corresponds to a separate UTXO. When it’s time to liquidate, you have to handle the whole coin; you can’t precisely remove 20%. So how users split their Vaults directly determines the granularity of liquidation. Putting 1 BTC into a big Vault is convenient to operate, but in a risk event the entire thing could be disposed of at once. Splitting into multiple smaller Vaults offers more flexibility, but it increases the costs of creating, managing, and proving them.

I think this is the layer of TBV that’s easy to overlook: it doesn’t simply copy Ethereum’s account model onto Bitcoin. Instead, it accepts the reality that UTXOs can’t be arbitrarily cut, and rebuilds collateral management around that constraint. Also, the Vault is bound to a specific application at creation time and can’t be freely moved to another protocol later. That can reduce the risk of assets being re-called or mixed, but you pay a price in liquidity and integration efficiency.

So when I look at TBV now, I don’t only ask whether the yield is high. 📰 U.S. oil reserves hit a 41-year low! Iran tensions escalate—BTC at $64,616 might be in trouble

Event overview

U.S. strategic petroleum reserves have fallen to the lowest level since 1983, and—just when things are heating up—tensions in Iran are also escalating. In plain terms, the “ammunition” the U.S. has on hand is running low. If fighting truly breaks out in the Middle East, there won’t be enough buffer stock to keep oil prices from surging. Oil price spikes → inflation expectations rise → risk assets are sold first. This logic chain is something every seasoned trader already understands. BTC is currently around $64,616.95, and ETH is around $1,929.06. It looks calm on the surface, but there are strong undercurrents beneath.

In-depth analysis

Why is this news important?

Honestly, a lot of people skim past “oil reserves” and think it has nothing to do with crypto. But dig deeper—

Is the U.S. strategic petroleum reserve meant to be used? Yes—it's the final ace for wartime or major crises. That ace is now thinner than ever in 41 years, which means that if something goes wrong on Iran’s side, the U.S. won’t have enough tools to stabilize oil prices. A sharp jump in oil prices would feed directly into inflation expectations, and those expectations are a core anchor for the Federal Reserve’s monetary policy.

What is the underlying logic in the entire crypto market right now? It’s betting on the Fed cutting rates. As long as rate-cut expectations are there, the liquidity narrative stays intact, and BTC can hold above the $60,000 area. But if a geopolitical conflict pushes oil prices higher, inflation expectations rebound, and rate cuts become unlikely—or even rate-hike expectations could return. That’s the real “killer move.”

Looking even bigger: the U.S. has been releasing strategic reserves on a large scale since 2022 to suppress oil prices. In essence, it’s consuming “family assets” to trade for political leverage. Now the reserves are near empty, replenishing them takes time and money—meaning the U.S.’s ability to manage oil prices will drop significantly over a long period. Markets hate uncertainty the most, and this situation is an amplifier of uncertainty.

Market impact

In the short term, this news won’t directly dump the market by itself, but it acts as a “risk catalyst.” BTC around the $64,616 level is already hesitating—down 0.11% over the past 24 hours—suggesting both bulls and bears are watching and waiting. If Iran takes any meaningful action—whether attacking oil fields or blockading straits—oil prices could jump instantly, and panic sentiment would quickly spread into crypto.

ETH is a bit more interesting: it’s up 1.82% over the past 24 hours. But such gains can be erased in one move once panic hits. ETH at ~$1,929 isn’t high, but if the broader market drops systemically, it won’t be able to escape.

Consider the early stage of the Russia-Ukraine conflict in 2022: within about two weeks, BTC fell from around $40,000 to $33,000—nearly a 20% move. Back then it was also oil spikes, inflation surging, and the Fed being forced to accelerate rate hikes. History won’t repeat exactly, but the timing feels similar.

Medium term: if tensions in the Middle East remain high, capital will keep rotating into safe-haven assets—gold, U.S. Treasuries, and the dollar. In the short term, crypto may be treated as a risk asset and sold alongside them. What’s interesting, though, is that after each geopolitical crisis, more and more people start to rediscover the “digital gold” narrative of BTC. The script of “down first, then up” shouldn’t be unfamiliar to old hands.

📰 美国石油储备创41年新低！伊朗局势升级BTC $64,616悬了

事件概述

美国战略石油储备已经跌到1983年以来的最低水平，偏偏这个时候伊朗局势又在升温。说白了就是美国手里的"弹药"快见底了，万一中东真打起来，没有足够的缓冲库存来压油价。油价飙升→通胀预期抬头→风险资产最先被抛，这条逻辑链老交易员都懂。BTC现在报$64,616.95，ETH报$1,929.06，看着平静，水面下暗流涌动。

深度解读

为什么这条新闻重要？

讲真，很多人看到"石油储备"三个字就划走了，觉得跟币圈有啥关系。但你要往深了想——

美国战略石油储备是干用的？就是战争或者重大危机时候的最后一张底牌。这张牌现在薄到41年最差，意味着什么？意味着一旦伊朗那边擦枪走火，美国没有足够的工具去平抑油价。油价暴涨直接传导到通胀预期，而通胀预期又是美联储货币政策的核心锚点。

现在整个加密市场的底层逻辑是什么？是赌美联储降息。降息预期在，流动性叙事就在，BTC就能撑住六万出头。但如果地缘冲突把油价打上去，通胀反弹，降息就别想了，甚至可能重新加息预期。这才是真正的杀招。

再往大了看，美国从2022年就开始大规模释放战略储备压油价，本质上是在消耗"祖产"来换政治筹码。现在储备见底，补库需要时间和金钱，这意味着未来很长一段时间美国对石油价格的调控能力大幅下降。市场最讨厌的就是不确定性，而这种情况就是不确定性的放大器。

对市场的影响

短期来看，这条新闻本身不会直接砸盘，但它是一个"风险催化剂"。BTC在$64,616这个位置本来就走得犹犹豫豫，24小时跌了0.11%，说明多空都在观望。一旦伊朗有任何实质性行动——不管是袭击油井还是封锁海峡——油价瞬间跳涨，市场恐慌情绪会迅速传导到加密。

ETH反而有点意思，24小时涨了1.82%，但这种涨幅在恐慌来临时可能一笔就抹掉。ETH现在$1,929的位置不算高，可如果大盘系统性下跌，它也跑不了。

参考2022年俄乌冲突初期，BTC在两周内从$4万附近砸到$3.3万，幅度接近20%。那次也是油价飙、通胀爆、美联储被迫加速加息。历史不会简单重复，但节奏很像。

中期来看，如果中东局势持续紧张，资金会继续往避险资产跑——黄金、美债、美元，加密货币短期内会被当成风险资产一起抛。但有意思的是，每次地缘危机之后，都会有越来越多的人开始重新理解BTC的"数字黄金"叙事。先跌后涨的剧本，老铁们应该不陌生。

操作思路

🎯 影响预判
- 币种：BTC / ETH
- 方向：利空📉 预测跌
- 时长：BTC 12小时 / ETH 24小时

💡 我的看法很直接：短线偏空，别急着抄底。BTC如果跌破$63,000这个心理关口，下方看到$60,000-61,000区间，那里才是比较舒服的接货位置。ETH如果守不住$1,900，$1,800是下一个支撑。现在的策略就是管住手，让子弹飞一会。地缘政治这种事，消息面一天一个样，别拿真金白银去赌方向。

Event Overview

Satellite images confirm that Saudi Aramco’s Abqaiq oil facilities were indeed damaged. Plainly put, this isn’t just a minor incident. Abqaiq is one of the world’s largest crude oil processing facilities, with daily processing capacity exceeding 7 million barrels. Back in 2019, Yemen’s Houthi forces blew it up once—at the time, global crude oil output instantly dropped by 5%, and oil prices surged by 15%.

Now that satellite evidence is out, the damage is real. The global energy market will almost certainly have some serious jitters next, and a spike in oil prices is basically a given.

In-Depth Analysis

Why is this news important?

Guys, the core logic is actually very simple—geopolitical conflict escalates → oil prices surge → inflation expectations heat up again → safe-haven assets become increasingly sought after.

Honestly, the timing is extremely delicate. The Fed has just begun its easing cycle. The market was already trading the narrative that “inflation is handled.” Then the Saudi oil facilities got blown up—equivalent to slapping that narrative directly in the face. If oil prices keep rising, inflation data could bounce at any time, and then the Fed’s rate-cut schedule will be thrown into doubt.

But in the short term, money won’t think that deeply. With tensions high in the Middle East, the instinct of traditional markets is to look for safe havens. Gold will rise, and the “digital gold” narrative for BTC will be reactivated.

Now look at the correlation—recently, the situation in the Middle East has been heating up. This attack on Saudi facilities is part of a chain reaction. Whenever geopolitical tensions escalate, BTC tends to see a safe-haven buy within the short term. In 2019, when Abqaig was attacked, BTC surged from $10,000 to $10,600 within two weeks.

Impact on the Market

Right now, BTC is at $65,241.63 and ETH at $1,957.93. To be frank, this level is crucial.

From a short-term sentiment perspective, this is absolutely a bullish catalyst. Oil prices jump → safe-haven funds pour in → BTC and ETH both benefit. Especially since ETH is already up 3.30% today, it suggests the money is already moving.

For the medium-term trend, we have to look at it in two layers: if Saudi Arabia quickly repairs the facilities, this will likely play out as a sentiment-driven impulse—rally first, then pull back. But if the repair timeline drags on, with oil prices staying elevated for longer, inflation expectations will fundamentally reshape how the market views the Fed. Then the impact becomes more complicated—it could rise first and fall later.

The most direct historical reference is the September 2019 attack. BTC did rise in the short term back then, but the sustainability wasn’t strong—safe-haven premium lasted about two weeks. This situation is similar, but the current macro environment is more complex. With the combination of an easing cycle and geopolitical conflict, volatility will likely be bigger than last time.

ETH’s performance deserves extra attention. ETH’s 3.30% gain today has already outperformed BTC’s 0.86%. If safe-haven sentiment continues to build, ETH’s upside momentum should be stronger.

Event overview

The Houthis are at it again. This time they hit Saudi Aramco’s Jazan refinery, and a fire has already broken out on site. In plain terms, it’s the people in the Middle East throwing missiles at each other again—only this time it landed on one of the world’s most critical oil facilities. Since Saudi Aramco isn’t just an ordinary company—one of the lifelines of global oil supply—an attack on the refinery could send oil prices surging again, and surging oil prices typically stoke inflation expectations. With BTC currently at $64,962 and ETH at $1,952.54, short-term safe-haven sentiment could flow directly into the crypto market.

In-depth analysis

Why is this news important?

Don’t think Middle East wars have nothing to do with trading coins. The logic chain here is actually pretty direct. Starting from late last year, the Houthis have frequently attacked shipping routes in the Red Sea and Saudi facilities. This time, they escalated again by striking a refinery and causing a fire. Once oil prices rise continuously, the Fed will have less room to cut rates—if inflation can’t be brought down, interest rates can’t move.

But this affects the crypto market in a two-sided way. In the short term, geopolitical conflict will boost safe-haven sentiment, and traditional funds may lean into the “digital gold” narrative. When BTC encounters a Middle East black swan, the initial reaction might be to drop along with the U.S. stock market—but the subsequent rebound often comes faster than with traditional assets. Back in April 2024, when Iran and Israel traded missile strikes, BTC first fell and then rose, reclaiming all losses within a week.

With ETH at $1,952.54 and up 3.57% over the past 24 hours, it suggests money has already been flowing back into the crypto market. If rising oil prices continue to fuel inflation narratives, inflation-hedging assets may return as the market’s main theme.

Market impact

The short-term impact chain is very clear: refinery fire → oil price jumps → inflation expectations heat up → funds seek safe-haven and anti-inflation targets → BTC benefits.

But honestly, there’s one risk point to watch: if oil prices surge and cause a major pullback in U.S. stocks, the crypto market will very likely drop alongside the stocks first. During the initial outbreak of the Russia-Ukraine conflict in 2022, BTC also tumbled by about 20% before slowly recovering. So in the short term, volatility is likely to expand significantly—it’s not a one-way climb.

However, looking at the medium-term trend, this event strengthens the narrative of BTC as a “non-sovereign safe-haven asset.” Especially after ETFs came in, the logic for institutional capital inflows has changed—there is much stronger willingness to buy the dip than before. ETH, meanwhile, benefits from the overall market sentiment improving. If ETH can hold above the $1,952 level, aiming for levels above $2,000 shouldn’t be a big issue.

📰 沙特炼油厂突发大火！胡塞武装再动手，BTC $64,962要变避险资产了

事件概述

胡塞武装又搞事了，这次直接打到了沙特阿美的吉赞炼油厂，现场已经起火。说白了就是中东那帮人又互相扔导弹了，只不过这次砸到了全球最重要的石油设施之一。沙特阿美不是普通公司，全球石油供应的命脉之一，炼油厂被打意味着油价可能又要飙，而油价飙=通胀预期升温。当前BTC在$64,962，ETH在$1,952.54，短期避险情绪可能直接传导到币圈。

深度解读

为什么这条新闻重要？

老铁们别觉得中东打仗跟咱炒币没关系，这里的逻辑链其实很直接。胡塞武装从去年底开始频繁袭击红海航线和沙特设施，但这次打到炼油厂起火，性质又升级了一层。油价一旦连续拉升，美联储降息的底气就更弱了——通胀压不下来，利率就别想动。

但这事对币圈是双面的。短期看，地缘冲突会推升避险情绪，传统资金会往"数字黄金"叙事上靠。BTC这东西每次遇到中东黑天鹅，第一反应虽然可能是跟着美股砸一下，但随后的反弹往往比传统资产更快。2024年4月伊朗以色列互扔导弹那次，BTC先跌后涨，一周就收复了全部失地。

ETH现在$1,952.54，24小时涨了3.57%，说明资金已经在往加密市场回流了。如果油价持续走高带动通胀叙事，抗通胀资产会重新成为市场主线。

对市场的影响

短期影响链路很清楚：炼油厂起火→油价跳涨→通胀预期升温→资金寻找避险和抗通胀标的→BTC受益。

但说实话这里面有个风险点要注意：如果油价暴涨导致美股大幅回调，币圈大概率会跟着美股一起先跳水。2022年俄乌冲突刚爆发时BTC就先暴跌了20%才慢慢回来。所以短期内波动率会明显放大，不是单向涨。

不过从中期趋势看，这次事件会强化BTC作为"非主权避险资产"的叙事。特别是ETF通过之后，机构资金流入的逻辑已经变了，逢低买入的意愿比以前强得多。ETH这边则受益于整体市场情绪回暖，$1,952这个位置如果站稳，后续看向$2,000以上问题不大。

#baby Do you remember what they said in physics class—“friction has nothing to do with the contact area”? That’s only an ideal model. In real life, once the tread pattern on a car tire wears down and the contact area gets smaller, the grip force drops immediately, and the braking distance stretches. The encrypted system works the same way: decentralization isn’t a switch you flip and it works right away; it’s a slope you have to climb higher and higher, and the effort gets heavier as you go.

When I was reading section 9 of the @babylonlabs_io  whitepaper about the multi-chain deployment strategy, the term “Bitcoin light client” kept catching my attention for a long time. Most people might think it’s just a standard technical component, but if you look closely, you’ll realize it’s the load-bearing wall of the entire cross-chain vault architecture. The light client’s job isn’t complicated: it doesn’t need to painstakingly sync hundreds of GB of a full-node ledger; it only downloads block headers, and then uses Merkle proofs to verify whether a given transaction was actually included in the Bitcoin mainnet.

This part is unavoidable. The subsequent mention of collBTC minting, as well as the generation of stablecoins, all depends on the light client to “witness with its own eyes”—proving that your Bitcoins are indeed locked in the mainnet vault in a proper, obedient way. In a multi-chain interoperability environment, without these eyes watching the mainnet, so-called cross-chain proofs and minimized trust become meaningless.

But here’s the problem: every time you add another chain, you need to recruit another batch of validator nodes to keep the network running. These nodes don’t have direct profits right now, but there are real, concrete costs for server and bandwidth operations. So who foots that bill? That depends on the token economics in section 10 of the whitepaper: $BABY . In the early stage, the gist is that the system subsidizes these infrastructure providers out of its own pocket—if you help the system “keep an eye,” the system pays you $BABY.

Viewed in isolation, a light client is like a boring middleware. But across dozens of chains, it’s the validation network woven by hundreds or thousands of light clients that truly becomes the vault’s real moat. Once the ecosystem matures and actual protocol fees can take over from early token subsidies, the transition from “burning money” to “earning money” can be completed. At that point, you’ll understand that $BABY  doesn’t generate value out of thin air—it is firmly anchored in the silent labor of nodes running day and night. #eth $ETH

Event Overview

Put simply, the Pentagon has reclassified the casualty numbers from Iran’s latest round of conflict, cutting the official death toll directly. On the surface they call it a “data revision,” but in reality they’re trying to make the conflict look less severe and reduce public-opinion pressure. But if people are really killed in the fighting, what difference does it make to change a number? This directly affects the direction of subsequent policies, and also throws market pricing of geopolitical risk completely out of whack.

In-Depth Analysis

Why is this news important?

Guys, the core of this news isn’t the casualty figures themselves—it’s why the Pentagon chose to change the data at this particular moment.

First, it indicates military actions toward Iran are escalating, and not on a small scale. If it were just minor friction, the Pentagon wouldn’t need to touch the data. Changing the numbers means the actual casualties far exceed what’s been officially disclosed, and they’re worried that backlash from the public will restrict policy.

Second, this is a classic wartime information-control move. In crypto markets, information asymmetry is the biggest risk source. Traditional institutions base decisions on official data, but on-chain capital and the news cycle have already spread it. When the official side starts “correcting” the data, anyone who’s traded for years knows—this is big trouble.

Third, looking at the current cycle, geopolitical conflict is one of the biggest black swans of 2024. BTC has been stuck around $64,773 for a day, and in 24 hours it only rose 0.06%—it can’t move. Market Impact

In the short term, this news will intensify risk-avoidance sentiment. The Pentagon’s move to alter casualty data is, in the eyes of seasoned traders, a “this is just like hiding something in plain sight.” If the casualties are supposedly reduced, then why do they need to reclassify it? The logic simply doesn’t hold.

Let’s map the impact chain:

When retail investors see the Iran headlines, their first reaction is to sell in search of safety. On the institutional side, risk exposure may be reduced because policy uncertainty is perceived as lower. In the derivatives market, if the long/short ratio becomes imbalanced, it sets up the domino script for liquidations. ETH is currently around $1,93.3; it’s only a few dollars away from the key support at $1,900—once that breaks, it’s a free-fall.

Looking back at history: whenever conflicts in the Middle East escalated last year, BTC’s average short-term pullback was about 4–6%. After feeding Dou Dou in the early morning, I happened to check the news. Bitmine has already accumulated 5.79 million ETH—about 4.8% of the circulating supply.

The background to all this isn’t complicated.

A lot of companies hoard coins, and what most people are familiar with is hoarding $BTC.

Now it’s channeling everything—company treasury holdings, staking, buybacks—into $ETH .

In plain terms, it wants to turn itself into a “super coin-holding company,” and it also gets to pocket the staking yield along the way.

Honestly, stories like this are the easiest to get people fired up.

Because it’s not just buying coins—it’s packaging “a company buys coins” as a kind of long-term allocation narrative, which sounds really high-level.

But watching it, I still feel a little uncomfortable.

$ETH  is currently 1954.88, up only 2.06% over the past 24 hours—not exactly crazy.

However, contract trading volume is already 14.5 times that of spot. Once this kind of hype kicks in, the order book can easily become inflated.

Drawing charts all day until your eyes hurt, and then alone staring at the candlesticks at night—I’m most afraid of this kind of situation: the story is huge, the price hasn’t fully caught up yet, and leverage gets crowded in first 😅

So my stance is very clear: I’m more of a wait-and-see, not chasing.

It’s not that Bitmine’s moves are useless—if anything, they’re just too easy to be used to sell a story.

If it really keeps gaining strength, I’d rather wait until it shakes out the emotions first.

The market turns on you faster than turning a page—keep some dry powder. $ETH #ETH

$SHIB  is back in the spotlight with a strong rally, but the move isn't being driven by a single event. Instead, it's a combination of improving market conditions and renewed interest in meme coins.

💹 Positive market sentiment. A broader crypto rally, stronger buying pressure, and improving investor confidence are supporting SHIB's price action.

A Look Back at SHIB's History

One of the most memorable moments in SHIB's history came when the development team sent 50% of the total SHIB supply to Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin.

In 2021, Vitalik donated a large portion of those tokens to India's COVID-19 relief efforts and later burned most of the remaining SHIB, permanently removing a significant amount from circulation.

⚠️ It's important to note that Vitalik did not create or distribute SHIB. The tokens were sent to him by the SHIB developers, and the decisions to donate and burn them were his own.

Bottom Line

Today's SHIB rally is being driven far more by Ethereum's strength, improving market sentiment, and renewed interest in meme coins than by historical events. If Ethereum maintains its bullish momentum, SHIB could continue attracting traders—but as always, meme coins remain highly volatile, so proper risk management is essential.

This doesn’t just affect oil prices; it’s also a heavy blow to the entire risk-asset market, including the crypto space. BTC is now $65,031.8, and ETH is at $1,944.27. Everything looks calm on the surface, but once this geopolitical fire gets going, sentiment can flip fast.

In-Depth Analysis

Why is this news important?

Honestly, the Strait of Hormuz isn’t a normal shipping route. Roughly 20% of global oil passes through here every day. If Iran blocks it or pulls tricks, oil prices could jump immediately, and inflation expectations would surge back.

What’s the broader backdrop right now? The Fed has just started hinting at rate cuts, and the market is betting on a soft landing. Iran’s move is basically pouring fuel on the inflation fire—oil prices spike, inflation rebounds, rate-cut expectations get dashed, and risk assets first take a hit and “bow out” accordingly. This logic chain is pretty straightforward.

And it’s not an isolated incident. Over the past six months, the Middle East hasn’t really calmed down—from the Red Sea shipping crisis to Houthi disruptions. Now Iran is stirring up trouble in the Strait of Hormuz again, and the fuse to the whole powder keg is getting shorter. For crypto markets, geopolitical conflict has historically been a short-term negative. Back in April, when Iran launched attacks on Israel, BTC briefly crashed from around $67,000 to below $61,000. This time there hasn’t been an actual attack, but Iran rejected the proposal on the negotiating table outright—its stance is clear, and further moves will be harder to predict.

Market Impact

In the short term, this news will accelerate capital flowing into safe-haven assets. Gold and U.S. Treasuries are favored; BTC and ETH—risk assets—will face continued pressure.

BTC is currently $65,031.8. If the situation deteriorates, $63,000 is the first line of defense. If that breaks, it could head straight for the $60,000 psychological level. ETH is even more uncomfortable: $1,944.27 is already below the $2,000 area where it has been consolidating. Capital outflows will become more obvious, and $1,850 could even be a target.

But in the medium term, if Iran is only playing edge-of-the-table games at the negotiation stage and there’s no real blockade of the strait, the drop might actually attract bargain-hunting capital afterward. After all, a blockade of the strait isn’t good for Iran either—they export oil using this route. Friends should understand this: the recovery speed after geopolitical noise-driven selloffs is often faster than you think. The key is to tell apart “a real war” from “issuing tough demands.”

【The dumbest mistake retail investors love to make: It has dropped this much—shouldn’t you be buying the dip?】

I know what you’re thinking—ETH is down from the highs by nearly half, and it’s still not even at two thousand dollars. So why aren’t you buying yet? What are you waiting for?

Hold on, though—I’m going to pour you some cold water.

$ 1940.66, 24-hour +1.5%, 7-day +2.3%. The numbers look good, but look closely—after almost a full week, it’s only moved this much. This isn’t a rebound; this is a struggle. 1871.99 is the lifeline—if it breaks, it won’t be range trading anymore; it’ll be the next step down.

But what’s interesting this time is: the Fear & Greed Index is only 30. The market is scared out of its mind—so in theory, it should keep getting hammered lower, right? Yet ETH is holding up right here. I’ve seen this kind of “it should drop but doesn’t”走势 more than once back in 2021. How it goes next? You’ve all seen it—there isn’t an immediate surge. It grinds, grind after grind, until most people give up completely—then it finally moves for real. So don’t rush to shout where the bottom is. It doesn’t matter.

Also, here’s a number for you to weigh: it’s down 61% from the peak. Sounds terrifying, but you have to ask—has the fundamentals collapsed? Has the ecosystem died? Has demand vanished? No. Valuation can always go lower, but it won’t go all the way to the end of the world. What this round cuts off is leverage—buyers who came in with FOMO, the ones who refuse to believe it and stubbornly hold on.

My own position? I tested with a light position. My stop loss was set right at 1871.99. It’s not because I’m bullish—it’s just because my hands are itchy—you know that kind of itch. But I didn’t go heavy, because the wounds from 2021 haven’t fully healed yet. I’m harder on myself than anyone, and my hands are steadier than anyone’s too—that’s muscle memory trained by the market.

Now it’s just waiting—waiting for the market to choose its direction on its own. What about you? Will you move this time? Or will you be like me—watching and itchy, but once you actually move, you get scared?

【散户最爱犯的蠢：跌这么多该抄底了吧？】

我懂你们在想什么——ETH从高点下来快腰斩了，现在才不到两千刀，这还不抄？等什么呢？

先别急，我给你们泼盆冷水。

$ 1940.66，24小时+1.5%，7天+2.3%。数据是好看，但你仔细品品——涨了快一周，也就涨了这么点。这不叫反弹，这叫挣扎。1871.99是命门，破了就不是震荡，是下一个台阶。

但这轮有意思的是：恐惧贪婪指数才30，市场怕成狗，按理说该继续砸对吧？偏偏ETH在这儿稳住了。这种“该跌不跌”的走法，我在2021年见过不止一次。后面怎么走的你们都看到了——不是马上涨，是磨，磨到大多数人彻底死心，然后才来真的。所以别急着喊底在哪，没意义。

还有个数字你们自己掂量：从高点跌了61%，听起来吓人，但你要问基本面崩了吗？生态死了吗？需求没了？都没。估值这东西，低了可以更低，但不会低到天荒地老。这轮下来，割的是杠杆，是FOMO进来的，是不信邪死扛的。

我自己的仓位？轻仓试了点，止损就卡在1871.99那个位置。不是我看多，是手痒——你们懂的那种痒。但我没重仓，因为2021年的伤还没好利索，说得比谁都狠，手比谁都稳，这才是被市场调教出来的肌肉记忆。

现在就是等，等市场自己选方向。你们呢？这波敢不敢动？还是跟我一样，光看着手痒，一动就怂？

translatedData.content:
I’m looking at BTCFi now, and the first thing I’m not even focused on is the annualized yield. Let me ask one question first: once this BTC is locked in, will it be promised again somewhere else for a second time? A lot of the risks don’t come from price falling. Instead, after the assets are wrapped, pooled, and reused repeatedly, the on-paper liquidity looks great—only when there’s real pressure do people realize everyone has been watching the same underlying collateral.
That’s also the most worth paying attention to after I re-researched @babylonlabs_io : Trustless Bitcoin Vaults. TBV isn’t about stuffing BTC into a public liquidity pool. It turns each Vault into an independent Bitcoin UTXO. BTC always remains on the Bitcoin network. The spend paths that are allowed are constrained by scripts and signatures at the time of creation; the protocol can’t move it elsewhere, and it can’t reuse it again as collateral. What’s read on the Ethereum side is the collateral state that can be used to make DeFi decisions—not another “shadow BTC” that can freely circulate.
This design lacks a bit of the sexy capital-reuse narrative, but it draws the risk boundaries much more clearly: which specific BTC corresponds to which Vault, which application it serves, and what conditions must be met for it to be liquidated can all be verified independently. For long-term holders, this may matter more than earning a few extra points in yield, because what really keeps people up at night isn’t whether the coins earn interest—it’s not knowing how many times the collateral has been used.
Of course, TBV is still on the testnet. Whether independent Vaults can maintain low costs and stable coordination as scale increases still needs to be validated by data. $BABY  is worth watching not just for how much BTC it can attract, but for whether it can help BTCFi move beyond the old problem of “one piece of collateral supporting multiple layers of credit.” #baby  #BTC #ETH

Brothers and sisters, Korea’s storage-chip giant SK Hynix has gone to list on the Nasdaq, with fundraising at a record $26.5 billion. In plain terms, it’s a super money-sucking machine. The U.S. stock market is already a bit shaky—once this big player goes public, global hot money will rush over. Honestly, SK Hynix is making AI compute chips. If it doesn’t get pulled from other places, it’s impossible. Over-the-counter funds in the crypto space will definitely be diverted.

Market impact
In the short term, this is a blatant bearish factor. IPOs in the traditional financial market act like bloodletting for the crypto market. With money limited, large funds will go to subscribe for SK Hynix shares, and the inflows into BTC and ETH spot ETFs will likely shrink. In other words, liquidity gets diverted, and crypto prices naturally face pressure.

In the medium term, global capital is rearranging its allocation. AI compute and cryptocurrencies are competing for limited liquidity. Market sentiment isn’t stable to begin with—fear/greed isn’t high—so big money is more inclined to embrace AI real-economy companies supported by performance, rather than highly volatile crypto assets. 消息一出来，全球市场立刻进入警戒状态。油价波动是第一反应，但真正聪明的钱已经在想下一步——能源价格飙升会推高通胀预期，而通胀预期对BTC意味着什么，老铁们心里应该有数。

深度解读

为什么这条新闻重要？

讲真，这事儿不能只看表面。胡塞武装打沙特管道不是第一次了，但这次的时间节点特别敏感。当前全球市场正处于美联储政策预期的十字路口，通胀数据反复横跳，任何推高油价的突发事件都可能改变宏观叙事。

油价的逻辑链很清晰：管道被袭→供应中断预期→油价飙升→通胀压力加大→市场押注美联储不得不维持高利率更久→风险资产承压。但这里有个反直觉的点，BTC这次的剧本可能不一样。

为什么？因为经过这几年的演变，BTC在地缘冲突中的角色已经从"风险资产"逐渐向"避险替代品"切换。2024年以来每一次中东局势升级，BTC虽然短期会跟纳指一起抖一抖，但反弹速度明显快于传统风险资产。背后的根本原因是全球资金在寻找脱离主权风险的储值工具，而BTC恰好满足这个需求。

当前BTC在$64,924这个位置，24小时微涨0.38%，说明市场还没有完全消化这条消息的潜在影响。一旦油价真正拉升，避险资金会加速流入。

对市场的影响

短期来看，地缘冲突会造成一波恐慌性抛售，这是刻在市场DNA里的反应。BTC可能会短暂下探，但下方支撑很硬。ETH目前在$1,944，24小时涨了1.68%，表现略强于大盘，说明山寨资金已经开始提前布局风险偏好回升的预期。

中期才是真正有意思的部分。如果沙特管道确实受损严重，油价持续高位运行，通胀数据会再次爆表。这时候市场会出现两个阵营：一部分人抛售风险资产避险，另一部分人把BTC当成数字黄金来对冲法币贬值。从过去几次地缘危机的经验看，后者的话语权在不断增强。

2022年俄乌冲突初期，BTC短期从$44,000附近跌到$35,000，但随后三个月反弹超过30%。这次如果胡塞的行动升级，类似剧本可能重演，只是节奏会更快，因为现在市场对"地缘冲突买BTC"这个逻辑已经有了共识。

Event Overview

Put simply, Iran and Oman are negotiating to resume navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. How crucial is this strait? Roughly one-third of the world’s seaborne oil passes through it. In the past, geopolitical tensions had markets worried that the strait could be blocked—oil prices would spike and risk assets would take a hit. Now that both sides have sat down to talk, the market’s biggest fear is that the “black swan” won’t be able to fly for the time being.

In-Depth Analysis

Why is this news important?

Guys, think about why BTC has been grinding repeatedly over the past few weeks. Besides liquidity conditions, the biggest external variable has been the Middle East. If the Strait of Hormuz gets squeezed, the transmission is very clear: oil prices surge → inflation expectations heat up → Fed rate cuts get derailed → risk assets get smashed. There’s no need to guess—every time geopolitics flares up, the same chain reaction repeats.

What does it mean that Iran is proactively talking to Oman to restore shipping?

It suggests Iran also doesn’t want things to spiral out of control. Most likely, the economic pressure from sanctions is too heavy and they need a step-down. Neighboring Arab countries also don’t want to be dragged into the fire. Honestly, geopolitical tensions cooling down is a real, tangible positive for the crypto market—not some fake story.

Looking at the current node, BTC has been repeatedly testing around $65,055, while ETH at $1,950 struggles to climb higher. The market doesn’t lack money—it lacks a reason that lets big capital feel comfortable returning. If Hormuz de-escalates, that could be the catalyst.

Impact on the Market

In the short term, this news directly suppresses panic sentiment and pushes funds back into risk assets. BTC is already up slightly today by 0.56% to $65,055.99, while ETH is up 1.90% to $1,950.42—the price action is already responding.

The medium-term logic is longer but the direction is clear: shipping resumes → oil prices stabilize → inflation data improves → rate-cut expectations revive → liquidity expectations turn better → valuation repair for BTC and ETH. This chain may not play out in a single day, but smart money will price it in ahead of time.

For reference from history: back in 2023, when Iran and Saudi Arabia reached a reconciliation in Beijing, BTC then saw a decent rebound over the following weeks. This time isn’t on that same scale, but the core logic is the same—geopolitical risk premium falls, and risk assets naturally benefit.

title: Les secteurs crypto qui pourraient dominer le prochain cycle haussier.
subTitle:
Chaque cycle haussier a ses gagnants. En 2017, les ICO étaient au centre de toutes les attentions. En 2021, la DeFi, les NFT et le métavers ont connu une croissance spectaculaire. Alors que le marché évolue, une question revient souvent : 
Quels seront les secteurs qui attireront le plus de capitaux lors du prochain bull market ?
Voici les domaines qui méritent une attention particulière.

1. L'intelligence artificielle (IA)
L'IA transforme déjà de nombreux secteurs, et la blockchain n'échappe pas à cette tendance. Les projets qui combinent intelligence artificielle, traitement des données et décentralisation attirent un intérêt croissant. Si cette dynamique se poursuit, les tokens liés à l'IA pourraient rester parmi les plus surveillés du marché.

2. Les Real World Assets (RWA)
La tokenisation des actifs du monde réel est considérée comme l'une des évolutions les plus prometteuses de la blockchain. Immobilier, obligations, matières premières ou encore œuvres d'art peuvent être représentés sous forme de tokens, rendant ces actifs plus accessibles et plus liquides.
Ce secteur pourrait favoriser une adoption plus large des technologies blockchain par les institutions financières.

3. La finance décentralisée (DeFi)
La DeFi continue de se développer. Prêts, emprunts, staking et échanges décentralisés offrent des alternatives aux services financiers traditionnels. Les projets qui privilégient la sécurité, la simplicité d'utilisation et une réelle utilité pourraient continuer à attirer des utilisateurs et des investisseurs.

4. Le DePIN
Les réseaux d'infrastructures physiques décentralisées (DePIN) proposent une nouvelle approche où les utilisateurs contribuent à des infrastructures comme le stockage, les réseaux sans fil ou la puissance de calcul, tout en étant récompensés.
Ce modèle économique attire de plus en plus d'attention grâce à son potentiel d'utilisation dans le monde réel.

5. Les infrastructures blockchain
À mesure que l'écosystème crypto grandit, les besoins en solutions de mise à l'échelle, d'interopérabilité et de sécurité deviennent plus importants. Les projets qui améliorent les performances des blockchains pourraient jouer un rôle clé dans le prochain cycle.

Comment identifier les projets les plus solides ?
Avant d'investir, il est utile d'évaluer plusieurs critères :
L'utilité réelle du projet.
La qualité de l'équipe de développement.La communauté et le niveau d'adoption.Les partenariats stratégiques.La tokenomics et la gestion de l'offre.
Le potentiel d'un secteur ne garantit pas le succès de tous les projets qui en font partie. Une analyse approfondie reste essentielle.
Conclusion
Le prochain bull market ne sera probablement pas porté par un seul secteur. Plusieurs tendances pourraient évoluer en parallèle, chacune répondant à des besoins différents de l'écosystème.
Les investisseurs qui prennent le temps de comprendre ces secteurs aujourd'hui seront peut-être mieux préparés lorsque le marché retrouvera une forte dynamique.

Et vous, quel secteur pensez-vous dominera le prochain bull market : IA, RWA, DeFi, DePIN ou infrastructures blockchain ? Partagez votre avis en commentaire !

ETH is now at 1947, down from 1982.

I’ve said this eight times already: the order book becomes thinner with lighter trading volume, and it gets hard-pulled up to 1982. Now the order book is finally thicker—buy orders are twice the sell orders—yet the price is dropping instead. Every time I think I understand it, it turns around and slaps me in the face. I really can’t figure this out.

On-chain, there are 98% fewer people borrowing money, and open positions are also trending downward. But whale accounts are up by 10%, and each position is smaller—more people are opening longs, but with small orders. Retail longs are three times whale longs, and this area is still a bit crowded.

In the past three hours, all twelve money-flow lines are flowing in, but the price hasn’t moved. Trading volume is shrinking too. Previously, when the order book was thin, it could be pulled up—but now that the order book is thick, it’s falling. I’ve seen this script before.

My view is that the adjustment isn’t over yet. But honestly, I’ve been slapped by this script too many times. Every time I believe it, it does the opposite. If it pulls back up again this time, then I’ll accept it too. No matter how you trade, it’s wrong.

【When everyone thinks it’s still going to drop, the market often starts to change】

Do you have this feeling—now when you open the charts, it’s nothing but fear everywhere, nothing but “it’s going to drop more” “it hasn’t bottomed yet,” yet ETH just keeps swaying and somehow holds its ground.

Honestly, this spot reminds me less of technical indicators, and more of the mindset after being cut in 2017. Back then, everyone said it was over—so what happened later? When it eventually rose back, there were actually fewer people on site who dared to chase.

The situation now is somewhat similar. Look at the data—the Fear & Greed Index is only 30; market sentiment is that bad. But ETH has refused to continue falling. Trading volume has also blown up abnormally—what does that mean? On one side, someone is frantically dumping at this level; on the other, someone is frantically buying it up. These two groups are actively exchanging positions—let’s see who can’t hold out first.

From the ATH, it’s down 61%. Isn’t that deep enough? Valuation is indeed in a low range. But low valuation doesn’t mean it will jump up right away—it only suggests that the room left for further downside may not be much.

On the daily chart, the line dividing bulls and bears sits in the range of 1874 to 2013. The current price is stuck in the middle—can’t go up, can’t come down. This kind of sideways consolidation won’t last too long, at most 48 to 72 hours, and a direction will be chosen for sure.

My trading instinct tells me: this time it might move upward first for a while. But I’ve said it too—my trading instinct often gets it wrong, so I didn’t enter this time.

What about you? If you currently have positions, what mindset are you in? If you don’t have any, do you dare to get in? Are you itching to trade?

📰 伊朗封锁海峡警告引爆避险！BTC $65,003还能撑多久

事件概述

老铁们，中东又搞事了。伊朗直接放狠话：谁敢在霍尔木兹海峡搞封锁，冲突就升级。说白了全球三分之一石油运输从这过，伊朗这是掐着世界能源命脉在叫板。消息一出能源市场先炸了，加密这边也跟着遭殃，BTC在 $65,003.69 小跌0.49%，ETH更弱， $1,949.65 直接砸了1.91%。

深度解读

为什么这条新闻重要？

讲真，伊朗拿霍尔木兹海峡说事不是第一次了，但这次节点特别恶心。

当前全球市场本来就处于"一有风吹草动就跑路"的脆弱状态。美股震荡反复，通胀数据阴晴不定，情绪面薄得跟纸似的。伊朗这时候跳出来喊封锁海峡，等于往火药桶里扔烟头。

加密市场处境更微妙。BTC在 $65,003.69 横了有一阵，上不去下不来，多空都在等一个催化剂破局。地缘冲突这种黑天鹅，最容易被空头拿来砸盘。ETH那边更惨， $1,949.65 这个位置早就摇摇欲坠，反弹的劲头全泄了，资金在持续往外撤。

说白了伊朗喊话本质是在博弈，想通过制造紧张换谈判筹码。但市场不会等你搞清楚是真打还是嘴炮——资金会先用脚投票。参考之前中东每次搞事，BTC都是先被砸一波再说，避险叙事短期根本不存在。

对市场的影响
